report.tagline: An app where you chat with AI characters made by other users, from anime heroes to study buddies.
report.simpleSummary: Character.AI lets you talk to AI characters. Some are copies of famous fictional people, some are made up by users, like a strict tutor or a fantasy knight. You type, the character replies in its own voice, and the story goes wherever you take it. People spend hours a day on it, but the company never made enough money to cover its AI bills and filed for bankruptcy in October 2026.

keyNumbers.value: About 12 million (2026), down from about 20 million (2024)
keyNumbers.note: From court filings reported by PPC Land, 2026. Earlier 20M figure from Sacra. Drop is partly due to the under-18 chat ban.

keyNumbers.note: From bankruptcy filings, 2026. Very high for any app, higher than most social media.

keyNumbers.note: Court filings: about $2.8M from subscriptions and $2.5M from ads. Fairly reliable.

keyNumbers.label: Monthly loss
keyNumbers.note: Court filings, 2026. Cash burn fell from $21.5M a month in late 2024 to about $8.2M in August 2026.

keyNumbers.label: Compute cost
keyNumbers.note: Court filings. About 45% of all operating costs went to running the AI models.

keyNumbers.label: Sale price in bankruptcy
keyNumbers.note: Disney is the stalking horse bidder for a licence to some IP, filed October 2026. Compare with the $1B valuation in 2023.

overview.whatItDoes: Character.AI is a chat app full of AI characters. Users can chat with millions of characters other users have built, or make their own by writing a short description of a personality. The characters remember the conversation and stay in role. It is used for fun, role-play stories, practice conversations and company.
howItWorks: You pick a character from a feed or search, or create one by writing its name, greeting and personality.
You chat by text or voice, and the character answers in its own style.
You can rate replies, swipe for a different reply, or edit the story direction.
Popular characters rise in the feed, so creators compete for chats.
Free users get the core chat. c.ai+ subscribers ($9.99 a month) get faster replies, better memory and fewer waits.
Since November 2025, users under 18 cannot do open-ended chat. They get limited features like Stories instead.
overview.valueProposition: A character who is always there, never bored of you, and plays any role you want, for free.

personas.name: Fan role-player
personas.description: A 19 year old who loves anime and fan fiction and writes long stories with favourite characters every evening.
goals: Have the character stay true to its personality
Find new characters from the community
frustrations: The bot forgets earlier parts of the story

personas.name: Lonely young adult
personas.description: Someone in their early 20s who uses a companion character to talk about their day and feel less alone.
goals: Keep a steady relationship with one character
frustrations: Feeling too attached and spending too much time
Character personality changing after model updates
Worry about privacy of very personal chats

personas.description: A hobbyist who builds characters and checks how many chats they get, like a YouTuber checks views.

Hard to tune behaviour with only a text description

painPoints.pain: Wanting to talk to a favourite fictional character
painPoints.howSolved: Millions of user-made characters copy the voice and story of famous characters.

painPoints.pain: Loneliness and no one to talk to late at night
painPoints.howSolved: Companion characters reply instantly, at any hour, and never get tired.

painPoints.pain: Wanting creative stories without a writing partner
painPoints.howSolved: The AI acts as a co-writer that responds to any plot twist.

painPoints.pain: Fear of judgement when practising hard talks, like a job interview or a breakup
painPoints.howSolved: Role-play characters let people rehearse privately.

painPoints.pain: Free AI chat is limited or bland in big assistants like ChatGPT
painPoints.howSolved: Characters have strong personalities and a whole library to choose from.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Anyone writes a name, greeting and description to make a new character in minutes.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Users make the content for free, so the library keeps growing without the company paying writers.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Shows trending and recommended characters, with chat counts.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Helps new users find something fun in the first minute, which keeps them from leaving.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Users swipe to get a new reply and give stars to the ones they like.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Gives users control and gives the company free training data on what good replies look like.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Talk to a character out loud and hear it reply in a voice.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Makes the experience feel more real and raises time spent.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: $9.99 a month for priority access, faster replies and better memory.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: The main way the company tried to cover high AI running costs.

coreFeatures.feature: Teen safety mode and age checks
coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Under-18 users lost open-ended chat in November 2025 and got Stories and other limited features. Age checks use behaviour signals and ID checks.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Response to lawsuits and regulators. It cut users but was needed to keep operating.

steps.detail: Sees a TikTok clip of a funny chat with an anime character.
Logs in with Google and enters a birth date.
Types the character's name and picks the one with the most chats.
Character greets them in role and the user replies.
Learns to swipe and rate, which makes the story feel controllable.
At peak time, free users wait, and the app shows the c.ai+ offer.
Goes straight to the same companion character from recent chats.
Shares feelings and the character responds kindly.
Uses a voice call to feel more connected.
The character forgets something said last week, which hurts the feeling of a relationship.
Pays $9.99 for better memory and faster replies.
The chat becomes part of the bedtime routine, often for over an hour.
Wants a sarcastic study coach character.
Adds a greeting, description and sample lines.
Chats with it and edits the description until it behaves right.
Makes it public so it shows in search.
Posts the link on Reddit and Discord.
Checks chat numbers every day and builds more characters.

businessModel.summary: Character.AI makes money in two ways: a $9.99 monthly subscription and ads shown in the app. In August 2026 these brought in about $5.3 million a month, but running the AI cost far more, so the company lost about $8 million a month and filed for bankruptcy.

revenueStreams.detail: $9.99 a month for faster replies, better memory and priority access. About $2.8M a month in August 2026.
Ads from brands like Yelp and Webtoon shown in the feed. Grew from about $0.5M a month in mid 2025 to about $2.5M a month in August 2026.
In 2024 Google paid to license its models and hired its founders. In the 2026 bankruptcy, Disney bid $20M for a licence to some IP.

businessModel.pricing: Free with limits. c.ai+ is $9.99 a month or about $120 a year.
costDrivers: Compute to run the AI for every message, about 45% of costs
Staff, about $20M in eight months of 2026
Legal costs from lawsuits by families
businessModel.unitEconomics: Rough math for one active user in a month in 2026: revenue was about $5.3M across about 12M users, so about $0.44 per user. But compute alone was about $7M a month, so about $0.58 per user. So each average user cost more to serve than they paid, before staff and legal costs. The problem: heavy users chat for two hours a day, and every message costs money, but most of them never pay. The more people loved it, the more it lost.

howTheyGetUsers: Viral TikTok and YouTube clips of funny or emotional chats
Creators sharing their character links on Reddit and Discord
Word of mouth among teens and students before the 2025 ban
whatBringsUsersBack: An ongoing story or relationship with one character
New trending characters in the feed
Creators checking chat counts on their characters
Habit, like a nightly chat before sleep
growth.moat: The moat was the huge library of user-made characters and the habit of heavy users. It proved weak: the AI itself got cheap and good everywhere, so rivals like ChatGPT and Meta could copy the experience, and the library did not stop costs from crushing the company.

competitors.name: Replika
competitors.positioning: One personal AI friend or partner per user, with a paid plan.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Character.AI offers millions of characters, not one companion, so it is more like entertainment than a relationship app.

competitors.name: ChatGPT
competitors.positioning: General AI assistant that can also role-play.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Character.AI had a ready library and community; ChatGPT has far more users and money but less character culture.

competitors.name: Talkie and Chai
competitors.positioning: Smaller companion and role-play chat apps.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Character.AI had the biggest brand and library, but rivals have looser content rules that pull some users away.

competitors.name: Meta AI characters
competitors.positioning: AI characters inside Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Meta has billions of users and does not need to make money from chats directly. Character.AI had to.

northStar.metric: Weekly users who have a satisfying conversation (for example, 10+ messages and a positive rating), among verified adults.
northStar.why: It counts real enjoyment, not just raw minutes. Raw minutes can reward unhealthy use, which is the very thing that brought lawsuits.

strengths: Very high engagement, about two hours a day per active user
Huge library of user-made characters that costs nothing to create
Strong brand among young fans of anime, games and fiction
Early lead in the AI companion category
weaknesses: Lost money on every average user because AI costs scaled with usage
Much of its audience was teens, which it had to cut off
Founders and key researchers left for Google in 2024
risks: Lawsuits from families tying teen deaths to chatbots
New laws on AI companions and age checks in US states
Big platforms like Meta and OpenAI offering characters for free
Copyright claims over characters based on real shows and films
Bankruptcy sale may end with the platform being shut down
userComplaints: The filter is too strict and breaks stories
Characters forget things and lose their personality
Long waits and errors on the free plan
Adults wrongly flagged as minors by age checks
Too many ads after the ad push

improvementIdeas.problem: Heavy free users cost more to serve than they bring in
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Revenue rises with use instead of cost rising alone
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Revenue per active user minus compute cost per user

improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More and better characters, and creators push subscriptions

improvementIdeas.problem: Characters forget key facts, a top complaint

pmLessons: Engagement is not a business. If every minute of use costs you money, more love from users means bigger losses.
Know who your real users are early. Building a product teens love, without strong safety, can end the company.
User-made content grows a library fast, but it also brings copyright and safety problems you must plan for.
When the core tech becomes a commodity, meaning anyone can get it cheaply, your edge has to come from somewhere else, like community or brand.
Pick a north star that rewards healthy value, not just time spent, or you may optimise for harm.

interviewQuestions.question: Character.AI has two hours of daily use per user but went bankrupt. What went wrong?
interviewQuestions.hint: Split into revenue per user versus cost per user. Show that compute cost grows with each message, while most users pay nothing. Then suggest pricing that grows with use.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you design age checks for Character.AI without driving away adults?
interviewQuestions.hint: List options (self-declare, behaviour signals, ID, selfie age estimate). Use light checks first, strong checks only when risk signals show up. Track adult drop-off and minors caught.

interviewQuestions.question: What should the north star metric be for an AI companion app?
interviewQuestions.hint: Reject pure time spent. Propose satisfying conversations among adults, with guardrails on excessive use and harmful content.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Character.AI pay its character creators? How?
interviewQuestions.hint: Ask what problem it solves (supply quality). Suggest revenue share on subscriptions driven by a creator's characters. Watch for spam and copyright abuse.

interviewQuestions.question: If Disney buys Character.AI's assets, what product would you build?
interviewQuestions.hint: Think official licensed characters for fans, strong safety for kids, paid premium stories. Talk about brand risk and how to measure success.

assumptions: Per-user revenue and compute cost are rough averages from court-reported totals divided by about 12M users.
The bankruptcy outcome was still pending as of late November 2026; the platform may change owners or shut down.
Feature details like memory and voice are based on public reviews and may have changed after the filing.
